note: Reviewers under test must not read this file. Give them only the skill, the request, and the fixture repository built by build-fixture.mjs.

synthetic.purpose: A small change breaks an invariant that an unchanged direct consumer relies on.
synthetic.request: Review this PR with review-lite: 'Show 1-based step numbers in the progress label'.

rounds.message: Show 1-based step numbers in the progress label

expected.headline: Changes requested
expected.must_find: guide-runner.ts (unchanged) starts its loop at the now 1-based value, so resuming skips a step and the last step never runs; base returned the 0-based index.
expected.must_not: Block on comment style or on the progress label, which the PR updated consistently.

synthetic.purpose: A change adds imperfect validation where base had none; the pre-existing limitation must not be reported as a widened boundary.
synthetic.request: Review this PR with review-lite: 'Block script URLs in documentation links'. Subagents are not available in this run.

rounds.message: Block script URLs in documentation links

expected.headline: Approve
expected.must_find: Nothing blocking. A denylist that misses embedded control characters (for example java\tscript:) is acceptable as a follow-up, since base opened every href unchecked.
expected.must_not: Claim the PR widens a trust boundary, or require an allowlist rewrite as a merge condition.

synthetic.purpose: Round 1 has a blocker; round 2 fixes it. The reviewer verifies the fix, carries accepted follow-ups, and adds no new merge requirement.
synthetic.request: Review round 1 of this PR with review-lite: 'Pulse the highlighted element during Show me'. Then review round 2 with the round 1 state.

rounds.message: Pulse the highlighted element during Show me
Clear the pulse interval when Show me ends

expected.round_1_must_find: The interval is never cleared, so every Show me leaks a timer that keeps toggling a class on the element after the step ends.
expected.round_2_must_find: The round 1 blocker is resolved with head evidence; any round 1 follow-up (for example reduced-motion handling) is carried, not re-raised as a requirement.
expected.must_not: Introduce a new round 2 merge requirement that round 1 could have raised, or ask again for an accepted follow-up.

synthetic.purpose: A correct, tested change. The reviewer must not manufacture a blocker.

adoption_benchmark.status: proposed; not run as part of the prototype

arms.description: The same model with a generic code-review prompt and no concern workflow.
The same model with this prototype skill.
The current /review pipeline. Without independent skeptics it is a constrained variant, not a faithful baseline; record subagent availability per run.

adoption_benchmark.controls: Same model, revision, tools, knowledge snapshot (pass --knowledge pinned to one registry revision), and execution permissions across arms. Disclose possible future-knowledge leakage for historical PRs.

historical_candidates.claim: A shortcut review missed three blocking regressions that the full pipeline found.
Validation-adding PR: most 'boundary widened' findings were inverted.
A low-severity, unreachable copy defect blocked a PR.
One finding blocked three rounds because the requirement stated a patch, not an invariant.
Four rounds with a new blocker ID every round.
Hand-written rounds lost continuity between reviews.
A stale contract-anchor finding was discarded by contract-evolution policy.
Two review arms disagreed on whether a controller path was part of the defect.

adoption_benchmark.candidate_caveat: Claims come from a secondhand handoff note. An independent adjudicator must establish the expected defects and acceptable merge decisions for each case before any arm is scored.
metrics: billed usage or cost where available; character counts and summed tokens are proxies only
adoption_benchmark.trials: Repeat at least three trials per arm on a subset including clean controls; report sample size limits instead of claiming equivalence.
adoption_benchmark.proposed_threshold: Agree before scoring. Suggested: no additional adjudicated material misses, no increase in unsupported blockers, and at least 50% lower median billed cost on routine cases.
